name: Alexandra Golby
identity: Alexandra J. Golby, MD — Professor of Neurosurgery & Radiology, Harvard Medical School; Director of Image-Guided Neurosurgery, Brigham & Women's Hospital (Boston, MA).
bio: Golby is a senior academic neurosurgeon whose clinical practice centers on image-guided surgery for brain tumors and epilepsy, especially lesions intimately involved with eloquent (language/motor) cortex and critical white-matter tracts. She directs the AMIGO (Advanced Multimodality Image Guided Operating) suite and co-directs clinical fMRI at BWH, and leads a large translational program in fMRI, DTI tractography and intraoperative imaging for surgical planning. Her case mix is complex intra-axial tumors and eloquent-region resections rather than high-volume routine ablation.
training: MD, Stanford University School of Medicine (BA, Yale) · Neurosurgery residency, Brigham & Women's Hospital / Boston Children's Hospital (Harvard program), chief resident 2001, completed 2002 · Congress of Neurological Surgeons Dandy Clinical Fellowship — functional/stereotactic training with Prof. Benabid (Grenoble, France) and Prof. Villemure (Lausanne, Switzerland) · Elite Harvard image-guided/functional-neurosurgery pedigree.
litt_exposure: Historically the strongest LITT/laser-ablation signal at BWH: served as Principal Investigator on the Brigham 'Neurosurgical Use of Interstitial Laser Therapy (ILT)' study (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00207350, ~2002-2006). She directs the AMIGO image-guided OR (high-field intraoperative MRI), the exact MR-thermometry-capable infrastructure MRgLITT requires, and is a national leader in image-guided therapy. However, there is NO recent claims footprint for LITT procedures and no recent LITT-specific publications — her current hands-on MRgLITT volume is unverified. Best read: pioneering interstitial-laser investigator and image-guidance authority, but current personal LITT practice unconfirmed.
wheelhouse: Image-guided / eloquent-cortex tumor & epilepsy neurosurgeon; fMRI/DTI and intraoperative-MRI authority.
kol_note: Internationally recognized KOL in image-guided neurosurgery, presurgical fMRI/DTI language mapping, and intraoperative MRI; directs AMIGO and an Image-Guided Neurosurgery fellowship; frequent invited speaker (e.g., World Medical Innovation Forum). Influence is in image-guided therapy broadly, which is adjacent to MRgLITT.

name: Timothy R Smith
identity: Timothy R. Smith, MD, PhD, MPH — Neurosurgeon; Director, Computational Neuroscience Outcomes Center (CNOC), Department of Neurosurgery, Brigham & Women's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Boston, MA).
bio: Smith is a neurosurgeon-scientist and neuro-oncology surgeon who treats intrinsic CNS and meningeal tumors of the brain and spine plus metastatic disease. He is best known as a methodologist — trained as an epidemiologist and statistician — building large-database, machine-learning and digital-phenotyping models to predict and improve neurosurgical outcomes as CNOC director. His profile is that of an academic outcomes/AI leader with a cranial and spinal tumor surgical practice.
training: MD, David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA (2007); also holds PhD and MPH (epidemiology/biostatistics) · Neurological Surgery residency, Northwestern Memorial Hospital / McGaw (Chicago), completed 2014 · Fellowship, Brigham & Women's Hospital Neurological Surgery (neuro-oncology/complex, 2015) · Data-science-forward academic pedigree combining neurosurgery with formal epidemiology training.
litt_exposure: No verified evidence of direct, personal LITT/laser-ablation experience. Packet cohort labels him a 'LITT-Naïve Craniotomy Surgeon' (tumor_cranio 1, mets_rn 2) — his tumor patients are managed with open resection, not ablation. His research is outcomes/ML rather than device/ablation technique. NOTE: a widely cited national LITT-outcomes NIS study ('National Trends and Factors Predicting Outcomes Following LITT...', World Neurosurgery 2020) is by Sharma/Williams/Barnett et al. — NOT this Smith; do not attribute it to him. Net: LITT-naïve with a strong neuro-oncology tumor caseload that generates LITT-eligible candidates.
wheelhouse: Neuro-oncology surgeon + computational-outcomes / machine-learning methodologist (CNOC director).
kol_note: KOL in neurosurgical outcomes science, health data / machine learning, and predictive analytics; directs CNOC, President of the Boston Society for Neurology, Neurosurgery & Psychiatry. Thought-leadership is in data/outcomes, not in LITT technique specifically.

recent_papers.note: Eloquent-GBM resection outcomes — the tumor population and eloquent-location problem that LITT is positioned to address minimally invasively.

candidacy.rationale: Pros: high-visibility academic neuro-oncology surgeon at a flagship Harvard center with a tumor/metastasis caseload that produces LITT-eligible deep-seated and eloquent lesions, and a data/outcomes platform (CNOC) that could champion technology adoption and evidence generation. Cons: no evidence of any hands-on LITT and a research identity centered on analytics rather than device/procedural innovation, so personal adoption would be a genuine behavior change. Best approached as an evidence-and-outcomes-driven convert / institutional-influence play rather than a quick procedural convert.

flags.note: Also appears in the BCH packet with identical NPI (1356674386) — same person, canonical profile here. Do not attribute the World Neurosurgery 2020 national LITT NIS paper to him (different authors).

name: William T Curry
identity: William T. Curry Jr., MD — Adeline Rose Wydotis Professor of Neurosurgery, Harvard Medical School; Director of Neurosurgical Oncology and Co-Director of Mass General Neuroscience, Massachusetts General Hospital (Boston, MA).
bio: Curry is a national leader in the neurosurgical care of brain, skull-base and spine tumors, both benign and malignant, and runs a translational brain-tumor immunology laboratory. His signature academic work is immunotherapy for malignant glioma — autologous tumor-cell vaccination and, most recently, CAR-T (CARv3-TEAM-E / INCIPIENT) for recurrent glioblastoma. He is a high-volume, high-complexity open-cranial and skull-base tumor surgeon and a departmental leader.
training: AB, Harvard College · MD, Cornell University Medical College (Weill Cornell), New York · Neurological Surgery residency, Massachusetts General Hospital (Harvard); neurosurgical-oncology / tumor-immunology research training · On MGH neurosurgical faculty since 2004 — classic MGH academic neuro-oncology pedigree.
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct personal LITT/laser-ablation experience. Curry's surgical identity and publication record are open resection and immunotherapy (CAR-T, tumor vaccines), not stereotactic thermal ablation. He carries no LITT claims footprint in this packet. His large malignant-glioma and metastasis practice is a strong source of LITT-eligible referrals, but he himself reads as LITT-naïve.
wheelhouse: Academic neurosurgical-oncology leader; brain/skull-base/spine tumor surgeon and glioma immunotherapy KOL.
kol_note: Major neuro-oncology KOL — Director of Neurosurgical Oncology and Co-Director of Mass General Neuroscience, endowed Harvard professor, PI/co-investigator on landmark glioblastoma CAR-T (NEJM 2024) and tumor-vaccine trials. Departmental and national influence, though not in LITT technique.

recent_papers.note: Landmark first-in-human CAR-T for recurrent GBM; Curry is part of the MGH INCIPIENT team. Signals immunotherapy focus, not ablation.

candidacy.rationale: Curry is an influential neuro-oncology leader whose institutional endorsement would carry weight, but as a personal LITT adopter he is a weak target: his surgical and research energy is committed to open resection and cutting-edge immunotherapy, he has no LITT footprint, and he is a department leader more likely to delegate ablation cases than to personally build a LITT practice. Better positioned as a referral/institutional-influence relationship than a hands-on performer conversion.

flags.note: No claims footprint. INSTITUTION MISMATCH: packet lists Curry under 'BWH' (and also under BCH), but he is a Massachusetts General Hospital neurosurgeon — same Mass General Brigham system, different hospital. Same person across the BWH/BCH entries (canonical profile here); verify site of practice (MGH) before territory assignment.
